text:
Alex M: FYI eu-west1c showing a weird eviction spike + lots of tiny GPU pods Pending, looks like fragmentation + attach latency.
Priya S: Saw the alerts. Is this the usual warm-pool gap or something new? :thinking:
Devon: Running a quick `kubectl get pods -n ml-prod | grep Pending` — most are tiny (0.5GPU) and waiting on attach/volume.
Devon: ```
NAME                         READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
inference-worker-rcp2z      0/1     Pending   0          2m
trainer-mini-8k             0/1     Pending   0          1m
```
Mai: I got node logs from the attach helper, saw timeouts hitting 60s and then preempt triggering. suspect NAT/conntrack backlog delays during burst provisioning.
Alex M: Interesting. We usually blame binpacking/fragmentation, but attach latency from egress saturation could block attach -> node marked unschedulable -> preempt churn.
Priya S: Any correlation with NAT gateway metrics or egress errors on those AZs?
sre-bot: [alert] eu-west1c: net-conntrack-utilization=92% across nat-gateway-2 — attach latencies spiked at 14:03 UTC
Devon: Here's the kubelet attach log snippet: ```
E0303 14:03:12 kubelet.go:123] failed to attach volume: timeout waiting for attach: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
``` 
Mai: That RPC timeout explains a lot. Small pods waiting for attach hold onto tiny GPU slots and cluster starts preempting to make room -> fragmentation worsens.
Alex M: So two vectors: scheduling fragmentation (many small pods) + infra egress bottleneck increasing attach time -> more preempts. We need short-term and medium-term fixes.
Priya S: Short-term: throttle burst rate from scale controller + bump warm-pool min for eu-west1c to avoid too many cold attach ops.
Devon: Also can we add a scheduler soft-affinity to prefer nodes with healthy attach latencies? maybe add nodeLabel egressHealthy:true set by an e2e probe.
Mai: Patch idea (short): increase warm pool min from 4 -> 8 for eu-west1c, and add a 30s backoff in the scaler to smooth spikes.
Alex M: Cost tradeoff noted: warm pool bump ~ +12% infra spend for region peak, but avoids repeated preempt churn which is worse.
Priya S: Medium term: route more attach ops through a second nat-gateway / scale nat capacity or enable egress-preserving path for attach RPCs.
Devon: Also a scheduler improvement: preferSameRack/az for tiny-gpu pods to reduce cross-az egress and kv/attach hops.
ops-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/attach-timeout — recommends checking nat conntrack and warm pool.
Alex M: I'll open a quick rollout: 1) scale warm pool min -> 8 (eu-west1c) 2) add 30s throttle to ml-scale-controller 3) temporary nodeLabel probe to mark low-attach nodes 4) monitor preempt rate and conntrack.
Priya S: Ack, will own the scaler throttle PR.
Devon: I'll coordinate NAT capacity spike with cloud infra team — may do an on-demand nat scale or failover.
Mai: After patch, we should run a small chaos test: burst 200 tiny pods and watch attach latency and preempt rate. :white_check_mark:
Alex M: Good. If anything changes or eviction rate climbs, ping #eng-oncall and I'll join.
Priya S: adding to today's ops board and linking cost estimate.
sre-bot: [note] Action items created: #5432 (warm-pool bump), #5433 (scaler throttle), #5434 (nat-capacity request)
Devon: quick note — avoid persistent forced binpack changes; prefer temporary warm pool+egress fix then evaluate scheduler tweaks.
Mai: Agreed. Will post results of the chaos run here in ~45m.
Alex M: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
